najena: The wiki page for this zone is actively maintained, and that is unique among the dungeons surveyed so far. It was edited ten times on 30 July 2026, between 09:30 and 11:01, by a single editor working through it. The Map section was separately expanded on 6 July and again on 24 July. Compare the rest of the project: The Hole was last touched 15 July, Befallen 7 June, The Warrens 16 May. The structured data behind this survey is hours old, not months.

The usual caveat still applies to the prose, and here it is unusually easy to see. The page began life on 30 July 2025 as a Project 1999 import. The narrative sections still carry that text word for word — the sentence about which keys are No Rent appears verbatim on Allakhazam, and the hedge about Journeyman's Boots ends in a literal question mark. So the split holds: infobox, map list, NPC table and item table are live Legends data; the Dangers, Keys and Traveling prose are classic EverQuest. Where the two disagree below, the structured record wins and the disagreement is shown rather than hidden.

Two other plotted pairs land on top of each other, and both are correct. BoneCracker and Trazdon sit 13.5 pixels apart — the map lists them as rooms 8 and 7, adjacent. Moosh and the injured halfling sit 15.5 pixels apart, both inside the prison. Neither is a plotting error.

One record does contradict itself and is not plotted where the wiki puts it. Rathyl reincarnate is listed at −154, −119, but the same page states he spawns on Rathyl's corpse — and Rathyl is at −670, −119. The X matches exactly and the Y differs by 516, which looks like a transcription slip. Expect him where Rathyl died, not at the listed coordinate. He is plotted at the listed value with this warning attached.

The spawn percentages below are almost certainly meaningless in Legends, and they are left printed rather than deleted. Four sources now say this zone has no placeholders, and the percentages only mean something if it does.
  • The 23 June 2026 revamp patch note — official, and the strongest source we have — promises “a striking lack of placeholders for named mobs”. This survey has quoted that line in section 01 since it was written, while publishing the percentages below.
  • eqlwiki Category:Named Mobs: “In EQLegends, named mob placeholders do not spawn in the revamped dungeons (e.g., Befallen, Blackburrow, Najena); the named mob(s) will spawn every time.” Added 10 July 2026 by Caliente, revision 155553 — eighteen days before launch, so it is a statement of intent rather than an observation, and the page is a Project 1999 import by origin — its oldest revision is from February 2019.
  • Avenrae, 9 August 2026: named respawned every cycle across 10 or more consecutive cycles while camping The Tenderizer for the Kitchen Toolbelt, with no placeholder seen. The same held over hours in Befallen and Blackburrow. First-hand and unconfirmed: this is a report of play, not a parsed log, and it is recorded as such.
  • Against all of the above, individual eqlwiki mob pages still describe placeholders in the present tense — Drelzna’s says “Her placeholder is a necromancer that spawns in front of the chair”. That is classic text nobody has been back to correct, and it is the only source of the four that disagrees.
What would settle it outright: a combat log across several cycles at one camp, showing the named on every spawn. That is Tier M and it is one evening’s play. Until then the figures stay on the page, struck through in meaning if not in ink, because deleting them would hide what the source actually says.

Why this survey now separates two respawn numbers. The header carried 19:00 as the zone respawn and argued it was current. It is not a zone figure at all: it comes from the wiki zone page’s prose, on a page carrying {{Classic Era}}, so by our own standard it is import text. The zone spawn timer in the same page’s infobox is 4:50, corrected there on 4 August 2026. The ~19 minute figure is a per-mob cycle, which several named records repeat independently, and it is kept as that. Publishing a T5 prose number in a structured field, and then reasoning about whether it was current, is the exact mistake this site exists to catch.

Port levels remain unresolved across the project. The eqlwiki Rituals page and the Travel Guide page disagree on druid and wizard port levels, and the Travel Guide has already been proven wrong about translocator routes. This survey does not quote a specific level for that reason. Gnoll Guard's spell pages are the likeliest source to settle it, since its spell data was rebuilt from the game client as of the 27 July patch with per-class level requirements verified field by field.

warrens: This zone's wiki page is thinner than it looks. It was created on 12 February 2024 as an import from the Project 1999 wiki and has been edited exactly three times since — most recently 16 May 2026, ten weeks before launch. The only substantive Legends edit was a note that the zone is available from the start. As with The Hole, the page's infobox and its NPC and item tables carry live Legends data because they are generated from the wiki's structured records rather than typed by hand; the ZEM shows the June rebalance and the item entries carry EQL stats and focus effects. The plot validates itself. Six pairs of named land within twenty pixels of each other, and every one of those pairs is documented as sharing a room — Smithy Rrarrgin with Foodmaster Rargnar in the Kitchen, King Gragnar with High Shaman Drogik in the Throne Room, Grodl Ripclaw beside the Muglwump, Aderius Rhenar with Koajin among the prisoners, Warlord Drrig next door to Lorekeeper Roggik, and Packmaster Dledsh beside the Prison Area. Coordinates and room list agree independently, which is the best evidence available that both are sound.

Three coordinates in the wiki's NPC table are out of range. A greater shaman is listed at 33% each at (−642, −2732), (−4205, 3319) and (−4313, 3336). Every other position in the zone falls inside roughly ±1200 on both axes, so these three are either mis-entered or belong to a different zone. They are not plotted. Treat the greater shaman as unlocated and expect to find it among the deeper shaman population.
